title: Bottom sheets stay open after you navigate away; the next tap only dismisses them
where: Phone: the hub's ••• action sheet (Suggest an improvement / Build it now / Import / Settings & rules) and Discover's Filters sheet
why: Open the sheet, then go Back or change route: the sheet floats over the new screen (Communities, the request page, Settings, Profile, Leaderboard). In the dark run it followed four route changes in a row, and the tap meant for 'New project' on Home was spent closing it. On desktop the same ••• menu closes correctly (project/desk-suggest-menu-after-back.png).
repro: Phone app shape: open #app/book-club-d10610/workshop, tap the hub's ••• (#dev-plus-btn), then go Back (history.back) or set location.hash to #communities / #settings. Same with #apps > Filters, then #leaderboard/challenges.

title: Escape in 'Who says yes?' closes the whole New project dialog and throws away the typed idea
where: New project dialog > 'Who can change it: … Change' picker
why: Escape should close only the picker on top. It closes both layers and lands on Home; reopening shows an empty brief, so the description the person wrote is lost.
repro: #home > New project tile > type a brief in 'What should it do?' > Change > press Escape. Home is shown; reopen New project: the brief is empty.

title: Just opening Invite mints a 7-day link, and the project then reads 'Invite link out' in Communities
where: Hub > Invite pane; Communities list row subtitle
why: Looking at the Invite pane creates a live link (by design per invite-pane.tsx) even if nothing is copied or shared. Afterwards the Communities row for Watering Rota changed from '55m ago' to 'Invite link out', telling the owner an invite is out when none was sent. NOTE: this audit run did this to Watering Rota.
repro: Communities shows Watering Rota '55m ago'. Open #app/watering-rota-fba57e/workshop > Invite, close it without copying. Reload #communities: the row now says 'Invite link out'.

title: Vote pill says '2 of 1 yes vote' / '2/1 yes'
where: Request #1 thread (bot's 'I built this' message), its Change #3 row, and the Done card on Workshop > All items > By stage
why: More yeses than needed is shown as an impossible fraction. Once the threshold is met it should say 'Approved' or '2 yes', not '2 of 1'.
repro: Open #app/book-club-d10610/dev/issues/1 after the change merged; also Workshop > See all > By stage, Done column.

title: Notification text is cut mid-word with no ellipsis
where: Notifications sheet, Homeroom bot row: '…Tap File it under my mes'
why: The body is truncated server-side or by character count and shown without '…', so it reads like a typo and hides the instruction.
repro: Tap the bell (#notifications-btn); Unread tab, Watering Rota group.

title: Unread tab count disagreed with the unread dots in All
where: Notifications: 'Unread (1)' chip vs dotted rows on All
why: With 'Unread (1)' (one item listed), the All tab showed two dotted rows: '2 new messages in Book Club' and the bot's draft. A dotted row that is missing from Unread is confusing. Later the count read 2, so it may depend on timing.
repro: Bell > note the Unread count and rows > tap All > count rows with a dot.

title: Notification meta line truncates the time, and count bubbles are bare numbers
where: Row meta 'Book Club · #1 · Homeroom bot · 7m …'; grey '5' / '3' circles beside the bookmark on message rows
why: On a phone the timestamp is the part that gets cut. The count circles have no words (house style: '5 new').
repro: Bell > All.

title: Chat header buttons float over the first message bubbles
where: Top-right of the DM and group transcript: the ••• (Conversation actions) and members buttons
why: The buttons sit on the transcript with no band of their own, so they cover message text and bubble edges as you scroll.
repro: Open #messages/5 or #messages/6 on the phone shape; look at the top-right under the header.

title: Own-message action sheet in the group shows '@@audit_ada'
where: Long-press sheet header quoting your own message
why: Double '@'. In the DM the same header reads '@audit_ben', so the group path adds a second @ to an already-@ name.
repro: #messages/6, long-press 'Can someone remind me Wednesday?'.

title: People are named three ways, and the project channel has a different composer
where: Author labels and composer
why: Group: '@audit_cy'; DM and #general: 'audit_ben'. The project's #general composer is a paperclip + 'Type a message...' with square coloured avatars, while Messages uses + / 'Message…' / mic with round avatars. The same component looks different on different screens.
repro: Compare #messages/6, #messages/5 and Book Club > places > #general.

title: Old proposals route silently lands on the Hub
where: #app/book-club-d10610/dev/proposals
why: The link opens the Hub with no proposals list and no notice. Old links in notifications and chats lose their target. It should go to Workshop > All items > By stage, which is where proposals now live.
repro: Load #app/book-club-d10610/dev/proposals; location becomes /app/book-club-d10610/workshop showing the Hub.

title: Homeroom menu cuts 'Go to community' to 'Go to com…' when a decision is waiting
where: Feedback & info sheet inside a project, 'Go to com… 1 decision waiting on you'
why: The status phrase takes the row and the action label is cut mid-word. Put the status on a second line.
repro: Open #app/book-club-d10610 while a vote is waiting on you > Homeroom menu (#platform-mark-btn).

title: Report form truncates the child-safety reason
where: Report app > Reason list, first option 'Child safety: a minor at risk, or sexual…'
why: The most serious category is the only one cut off, on every shape, so its meaning is hidden. Let it wrap.
repro: Homeroom menu > Report app.

title: Request 'More actions' sheet uses mixed emoji and text glyphs as icons
where: Request #1 > ••• sheet: ✎ ⚑ 🏷 @ ⊘ ↑ 🔕 ⇄
why: Colour emoji (🏷, 🔕) sit beside monochrome glyphs, in colours (red, orange) that do not mean anything. Every other sheet uses the line icon set (for example the hub ••• sheet).
repro: #app/book-club-d10610/dev/issues/1 > More actions (•••).

title: Request thread: jump-to-latest chevron covers text; 'CHANGE #3 · HOMER…' label cut
where: Thread scrolled to top: round chevron over 'Built from the …' line; change header beside the status pill
why: The floating button sits on the text with no reserved space, and the change label is cut mid-word next to the pill.
repro: Open request #1, scroll #gc-thread-scroll to the top.

title: People pickers put a red 'Block' beside every search result
where: New message > Direct / Group > results rows: 'Message' / 'Add' and 'Block'
why: A destructive action shares the row with the primary one in a picker whose job is choosing someone. It is easy to mis-tap and loud for an action rarely wanted here. Move it to a row menu or the profile.
repro: #messages > New message (#messages-new) > Direct message > type 'aud'.

title: Stray blue caret under the selected segment
where: Settings > Appearance (under 'System', #drawer-theme-caret); Suggest an improvement > 'Where should this go?' (under 'Homeroom')
why: A small triangle pokes out below the control's border with nothing attached. It reads as a broken tooltip arrow.
repro: #settings/theme; or Homeroom menu > Suggest an improvement > Got it > Form.

title: Desktop Settings nav is too narrow and its label disagrees with the page
where: Settings left nav: 'Linked ph… 3 linked', 'Agent instructions…'; 'Account' lit while the page heading says 'Profile'
why: Labels are cut while the content pane has spare width, and the lit nav item does not match the heading.
repro: Open #settings on desktop.

title: Several large headings per page (Settings sub-pages, desktop Hub)
where: Account: 'Profile', 'Sign-in', 'Delete account' at 22px; Notifications: three big headings; desktop Hub: 'Hub' page title plus 'Book Club'
why: House style allows one large heading per page. Here every section is a hero-size title.
repro: #settings/account, #settings/alerts; #app/book-club-d10610/workshop on desktop.

title: You screen shows '0 live' and '0 challenges' tiles, titled 'Profile'
where: Top of the You tab
why: House style: a zero shows nothing. Two big zero tiles are the most prominent thing under the name. The tab is 'You' but the header says 'Profile', which is also a row lower down.
repro: Tap You (#platform-tab-me).

title: Communities filter chips clip 'Just you 1' at the screen edge
where: Chip row under 'Search your communities'
why: The last chip and its count are cut by the edge even when selected. Four short chips fit at 393 with tighter padding.
repro: #communities on phone; tap 'Just you'.

title: Leaderboard: GET /api/v4/leaderboard returns 404 on every load
where: #leaderboard/challenges (Challenges and Standings)
why: The runner logs 'http 404: /api/v4/leaderboard?page=1&per_page=25' on both shapes. Standings shows only 'No events have been published yet.', so a broken endpoint may be hidden behind an empty state.
repro: Load #leaderboard/challenges; watch network for /api/v4/leaderboard.

title: Discover Filters has a Type section with one chip, 'Other'
where: Discover > Filters > TYPE
why: A filter group with a single 'Other' option filters nothing useful and looks unfinished.
repro: #apps > Filters.

title: Workshop 'By stage' board breaks out of the page column
where: Workshop > All items > By stage
why: The board starts left of the 'Workshop' title and runs past the end of its rule, so title and content do not share an edge.
repro: #app/book-club-d10610/workshop > Workshop > See all > By stage.

title: Workshop shows an orange 'Couldn't take the screenshots' with no next step
where: Book Club > Workshop > What's happening > Up next
why: An error line about the bot's evidence with no action and no explanation for a member. It may be a local-stack artifact (no capture service), but the state itself has no recovery path.
repro: #app/book-club-d10610/workshop > Workshop while a change is in progress.

title: Desktop message hover toolbar sits far from a left-aligned message

why: The reaction/actions bar pins to the transcript's right edge, about 800px from the bubble it acts on, overlapping the row above. It is hard to tell which message it belongs to.
repro: #messages/6 on desktop, hover a message from someone else.

where: Suggest an improvement > Form > Cancel
why: Several lines of typed feedback and an auto-suggested title vanish on one tap, with no draft kept and no confirm.
repro: Homeroom menu > Suggest an improvement > Got it > Form > type in 'What should change?' > Cancel > reopen.

title: 'Who says yes?' picker does not match its row label and has an unexplained 'Now' pill
where: Row 'Who can change it: You or the group · Change' opens a sheet titled 'Who says yes?'; first card has a 'Now' pill
why: Two names for one setting, and 'Now' reads like a speed rather than 'current choice'.
repro: #home > New project > Change.

title: Edit profile: focusing Bio scrolls its label under the sheet's top edge
where: Edit profile sheet, Bio field label and counter '185/280'
why: The field label and counter are clipped at the top of the sheet while typing.
repro: You > Edit profile > tap Bio > type several lines.

title: Hub Invite pane's back arrow goes to a menu you never opened
where: Hub > Invite: back chevron 'Back to Book Club's menu'
why: Opened from the hub's Invite button, Back should return to the hub, not to the Feedback & info menu.
repro: #app/book-club-d10610/workshop > Invite > back chevron.

title: Console: snapdom warning every time the Homeroom menu opens; native-session warnings in the app shape
where: Console on opening #platform-mark-btn; Settings > Homeroom app
why: Opening the menu logs '[snapdom] Text in inline/table-cell elements kept its natural width…', so a page snapshot runs on every open (a cost even if never used). In the app shape every load logs '[native-chrome] native session establishment failed: This Homeroom app version must be updated for secure sign-in', and Settings > Homeroom app shows a red 'Could not load Homeroom app settings'. That is likely because the bridge is emulated here, but worth confirming on a real build. No console errors or exceptions were seen; the only HTTP failure was the leaderboard 404.
repro: Open the Homeroom menu on any screen; open #settings/usernode in the app shape.
